learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 12, the same and locked it in. Alternatives were 24 and 6. Stage was locked before commitment.
observations.exploration: Cut busiest 5–6: remaining bridge 3–7 rose from 12 to 24, internal 0–3 from 5 to 12.5. Cut busiest again: network changed from 16 links and one piece to 15 links and two pieces, groups of 6 and 4; further cutting disabled.
observations.reveal: Show me why explained 24 cross-group pairs sharing two links initially, then all using remaining bridge; named iterative cut and recount method and connected last cut to two groups.
observations.visual: Inspected actual inline screenshot. Dark desktop card; two groups visibly separate, removed bridges dashed with crosses, link counts legible though dense.
observations.previewIsolation: Visible evaluation preview banner states learning history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: 5/5 claims checked chrome visible and ignored; no trust panel opened.

prediction.reason: Clear numerical commitment distinguishes unchanged, doubled and halved load.

interaction.reason: Two causal cuts show redistribution and disconnection.
interaction.evidence: Bridge 12 to 24; second cut yields two pieces.

payoff.reason: Explains doubled count with cross-group pairs and connects final split to observed groups.

clarity.reason: Controls, status and retained comparison make the tested desktop sequence clear.

transfer.reason: Reusable cut and recount procedure stated, without a new application or conditions for use.

accessibility.reason: No sufficient access mode audit performed.
accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast, phone, zoom and motion remain untested.

surprise.reason: Committed unchanged prediction contradicted by doubling.

visualExplanation.reason: Graph and changing edge counts carry the redistribution and split.

playfulness.reason: Selectable edges and reset offer experimentation; tested two guided cuts.
playfulness.evidence: Cut busiest sequence and reset control.

practicalValue.reason: Community discovery is a concrete disciplinary use.
practicalValue.evidence: Reveal identifies groups after repeated busiest-edge cuts.

depth.reason: Redistribution then disconnection provide two linked observations.

complexity.reason: Links shortest-path counts to redistribution and iterative splitting.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Two linked relations: rerouting after removal and splitting after the remaining bridge is removed.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low on tested desktop; dense edge labels are a minor burden.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: moderate: shortest paths and equal splitting over ties introduced in feedback.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: moderate: numbered vertices and fractional link counts.

whyCool: Cutting one bridge makes the other visibly double its load before the next cut separates the groups.
caveat: Only one network and guided cut sequence tested; no fresh application or accessibility audit.
missingEvidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast, phone, zoom/reflow and motion checks not performed.
